title: Overcoming the Incentive Collapse Paradox
abstract: arXiv:2603.27049v3 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: AI-assisted task delegation is increasingly common, yet human effort in such systems is costly and typically unobserved. Recent work by Bastani and Cachon (2025); Sambasivan et al. (2021) shows that accuracy-based payment schemes suffer from incentive collapse: as AI accuracy improves, sustaining positive human effort requires unbounded payments. We study this phenomenon in a budget-constrained principal-agent framework with strategic human agents whose output accuracy depends on unobserved effort. Our first contribution is a general impossibility result showing that incentive collapse is not merely a limitation of simple linear payments, but arises for any payment rule based only on observed task accuracy.To overcome this barrier, we propose a sentinel-auditing payment mechanism that enforces a strictly positive and controllable level of human effort at finite cost, independent of AI accuracy. translated_abstract: AI辅助的任务委派日益普遍，然而在这类系统中，人类的努力成本高昂且通常无法被观测。Bastani和Cachon（2025）以及Sambasivan等人（2021）的最新研究表明，基于准确性的支付方案存在激励崩塌问题：随着AI准确性的提高，维持积极的人类努力需要无上限的支付。我们在一个预算受限的委托-代理框架中研究这一现象，其中策略性行动的人类代理的输出准确性取决于无法观测的努力程度。我们的第一个贡献是一个一般性的不可能性结果，表明激励崩塌不仅仅是简单线性支付的局限性，而是产生于任何仅基于观测任务准确性的支付规则。为了克服这一障碍，我们提出了一种哨兵审计支付机制，该机制能够以有限的成本强制执行严格为正且可控的人类努力水平，且不受AI准确性的影响。基于这种激励鲁棒的
tldr: 该论文证明了激励崩塌源于任何仅基于观测任务准确性的支付规则，并提出一种哨兵审计支付机制，能以有限成本维持严格为正且可控的人类努力水平，不受AI准确性的影响。
en_tdlr: This paper proves that incentive collapse arises for any payment rule based solely on observed task accuracy, and proposes a sentinel-auditing payment mechanism that enforces a strictly positive and controllable level of human effort at finite cost, independent of AI accuracy.
